title: Burn 0.22 cuts rebuild times and simplifies multi-backend AI code
friendlyTitle: Burn makes Rust AI projects faster to rebuild
summary: Burn 0.22 removes backend type parameters from its user-facing Rust API and lets the device select execution, with Tracel reporting 6.2× and 14.7× faster release rebuilds in two model-edit tests. The release also adds LoRA and QLoRA support, early ONNX export, reusable compilation caches and revised memory management.
friendlySummary: Burn 0.22 simplifies how developers choose computer hardware and made two test projects rebuild much faster. It also adds tools for adapting and exporting models.
whyItMatters: Shorter compile loops make Rust-based machine-learning development less cumbersome, while device-selected execution can keep application code portable across CPUs and GPUs. Existing users face substantial API and checkpoint migrations, and the early ONNX exporter does not yet cover every model.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Developers can spend less time waiting after code changes. Current Burn projects will need migration work, and some export features are still limited.
